_comment: Tuning for build_kb.py entity-resolution stage. Everything here is optional overrides on top of the automatic pipeline (concept-map -> node_aliases -> gazetteer -> modifier-strip -> unresolved).
_strip_note: Removed only from the START or END of a surface string, then resolution is retried. These do NOT distinguish one ritual entity from another. Semantic modifiers (dewasa, anak, bayi, massal, utuh, pangentas, panglukatan, ...) are deliberately absent so subtypes stay separate.
_strip_note_2026_09_23: Cardinal words widened from dua..enam (2-6) to satu..sepuluh (1-10), and 'batang' (stick/rod counter) added, after the quantity-in-entity-name bug found this session (see force_merge's _quantity_in_name_note) traced to sembilan_batang_kayu_cendana -- 'sembilan' (9) and 'batang' were both missing, so nothing stripped at all. Paired with the build_kb.py Resolver._strip() trailing-digit-symmetry fix same session. Deliberately NOT widened further (e.g. sebelas+, or other counters like 'ekor'/'utas'/'orang') without a concrete case in this corpus motivating it -- see the _quantity_in_name_note for why this stays scoped rather than speculative.
_deictic_words_note: Batch H (2026-09-21, conersation.md item #29). Demonstrative/anaphoric pronouns (a subset of strip_modifiers) that, sitting at a surface's leading/trailing boundary, never contribute a genuine alternate name -- 'kelompok ini' ('this group'), 'rurub sinom tadi' ('that rurub sinom just mentioned') are the extractor picking up an anaphoric reference within one sentence, not a synonym a real user would type. build_kb.py's get_ent() now skips recording such a surface as an alias (resolution itself -- force_merge / strip-and-retry -- still routes it to the correct entity exactly as before; this only suppresses the bot-facing 'also known as' listing). Added after confirming the same shape recurs beyond item #29's own kelompok_paksa_mahayana: rurub_sinom already carried 'rurub sinom tadi' as an alias for the identical reason.

force_merge._note: surface string (lowercase) -> canonical id, applied before everything else. Use sparingly for cases the concept map misses.
force_merge._quantity_in_name_note: 2026-09-23: build_kb.py's Resolver._strip() has an asymmetry bug (leading position gets both a digit-pattern check AND a strip_modifiers check; trailing position only gets the strip_modifiers check, never a digit check) -- so a TRAILING count ('... sebanyak 9 buah', '... sebanyak 250 biji') stops the trailing-strip loop dead as soon as it hits the bare number, leaving the count stuck mid-string instead of being fully stripped. Also strip_modifiers' cardinal-number word list only covers dua..enam (2-6), missing tujuh/delapan/sembilan/sepuluh+, and lacks 'batang' as a counter word -- so a LEADING word-form count like 'sembilan batang ...' isn't stripped at all. Not fixed here (a shared-code change with a much bigger blast radius across all 496 entities than this specific glossary-review pass) -- these 4 explicit entries are the scoped, human-reviewed workaround for the specific cases found 2026-09-22/23. If this class of bug recurs often, fixing the code path is worth a dedicated pass.
force_merge._honorific_prefix_note: 2026-09-22: 'sang' is already in strip_modifiers, but _strip() abandons the whole retry if the stripped remainder isn't ITSELF independently a concept-map/alias/gazetteer entry -- it never checks 'is this literally an existing entity's own canonical name'. So 'sang hyang prajapati' strips to 'hyang prajapati', that lookup fails (not its own gazetteer key), and resolve() falls back to treating the FULL ORIGINAL string as a new unresolved entity -- found via the referenced-but-ungrounded gap audit. Same shape as the quantity-in-name bug: scoped force_merge entries below, not a _strip()/_base_lookup() rewrite, since only these 2 of the 72 audited terms hit it.
force_merge._english_synonym_note: 2026-09-22: 'ether' is the plain English gloss for akasa (the KB's own akasa and lingga_sarira_pitara definitions both already write 'akasa (ether/ruang)') -- never registered as a gazetteer/alias surface for akasa itself, so it surfaced as a false gap in the same referenced-but-ungrounded audit. Different mechanism from the honorific-prefix note above (this one was never in strip_modifiers territory at all), same fix shape.
force_merge._morphological_variant_note: 2026-09-22: these 5 are alternate word-forms (verb/noun, spelling variant, or generic-vs-ritual name) of entities that already exist, found in the same gap audit -- each confirmed by that entity's OWN definition text explicitly naming the variant, not just my inference. 'ngeringkes' (bare verb) vs 'pangringkes' (nominalized form; def says 'disebut juga Upacara Pangringkesan', and a source-sentence note on sentence 900043 independently confirms the same wrapping-stage concept). 'pasucian' vs 'pabersihan' (def: 'juga disebut Pasucian'). 'kerik kuku' (bare form) vs 'pengerikan kuku' (nominalized form), same nail-scraping ritual. 'walantaga' vs 'ulantaga' (def: 'disebut juga walantaga'). 'umbi gadung' (generic ingredient name) vs 'umbi sikapa/sekapa' (its ritual-specific name; def opens 'Umbi gadung mentah yang dipakai...', and the source sentence itself parenthesizes 'umbi sikapa/sekapa (umbi gadung)'). 'suksmasarira' vs 'lingga sarira pitara' -- I'd flagged this one as an overlap rather than merging it myself (lingga_sarira_pitara's def already opens 'Lingga sarira (sukshma sarira) adalah...'), user confirmed 2026-09-22 they're the same concept and should be interchangeable.
force_merge._merajapati_note: 2026-09-23: user confirmed Merajapati (the cemetery-complex temple, glossary_review_master.md's 'Ritual buildings' section) is the same site as the pre-existing 'pura_mrajapti' entity -- three spellings (Merajapati/Mrajapti/Prajapati) of one temple. Distinct from 'hyang_prajapati', which is the GOD worshipped there (Hyang Prajapati = deity; Merajapati/Pura Mrajapti = the place), not touched by this merge. The drafted 'Merajapati' glossary line was removed rather than kept alongside this force_merge, since build_kb.py's glossary-definition step unconditionally overwrites the merged entity's definition with whatever glossary line resolves to its id -- keeping both would have clobbered pura_mrajapti's existing (better, extraction-sourced) definition with the shorter drafted one.
force_merge._dewa_duplicate_note: 2026-09-23: connectivity audit (audit_connectivity.py) caught two duplicates this session's glossary batch introduced by resolving to the WRONG existing spelling-variant entity instead of the corpus's main hub one. 'Wisnu' (my drafted glossary line) fuzzy-resolved to a pre-existing thin/isolated 'visnu' entity (bare gazetteer hit, zero relations) instead of the corpus's actual connected god entity 'dewa_wishnu' (broader: panca_dewata, richer Ngaben-specific definition) -- same god, three surface spellings (Wisnu/Visnu/Wishnu) that were never unified. 'Dewi' likewise duplicated the pre-existing 'bhatari' entity (my own drafted definition even says Dewi is bhatara/bhatari's female-counterpart term) instead of reusing it. Both drafted glossary lines were removed (keeping the richer pre-existing definitions untouched) and these two force_merge entries added so future mentions of either bare spelling route to the correct existing entity instead of recreating the duplicate on the next rebuild.
force_merge._mabersih_mati_note: 2026-09-23 connectivity audit: my own drafted 'Mabersih Mati' definition literally opened 'disebut juga Pabersihan Mati' -- it's the exact pre-existing pabersihan_mati entity (already the merge target of 4 other surface forms per an earlier batch), not a new concept. Merged, drafted glossary line removed.
force_merge._near_dup_batch1_note: 2026-09-23 near-duplicate-id triage (connectivity audit): 3 genuine verb/noun or duplicate-extraction pairs found and merged, keeping in each case the entity already cross-referenced elsewhere in the KB as canonical. mapradaksina (verb 'moving clockwise') = pradaksina (the ritual noun) itself, same shape as ngeringkes/pangringkes -- was FIRST added under broader_overrides by mistake (linked mapradaksina TO pradaksina as a parent instead of merging it, since broader_overrides doesn't collapse the two into one id), caught by re-checking Resolver.resolve() output directly and moved here. upacara_nyiramang_layon and nyiramang_layon are the same corpse-bathing ceremony extracted twice from different source sentences (one citing tempat penusangan, other daun dapdap -- both true, kept as the surviving entity's context). gulungan_sirih and gulungan_daun_sirih are both 'lekesan' (rolled betel leaf) with near-identical definitions; kept the one already linked to kawangen_jeriji, and the two pre-existing force_merge entries that pointed AT 'gulungan sirih' ('lubang uang kepeng'/'lubang satu uang kepeng') were repointed straight to 'gulungan daun sirih' too, since force_merge values aren't re-resolved recursively. NOT merged despite high string-similarity: panebusan vs penebusan (pre-existing, deliberately left separate in an earlier batch pending real evidence), upacara_ngaskara vs upacara_pengaskaran (possible verb/noun pair, but upacara_ngaskara's own definition looks generic/possibly mismatched and needs source verification first), and the ngaben/upacara_pengabenan/upacara_palebon_ngaben cluster (flagged for the project owner -- upacara_palebon_ngaben's own definition literally says it's just another term for ngaben used for Ksatria, but merging into the single most-referenced entity in the whole KB is higher blast-radius than a leaf merge).
force_merge._ngaskara_pengaskaran_note: 2026-09-23: user asked for a web cross-check before merging this pair. An external Balinese-ritual source (komangputra.com) explicitly parenthesizes 'Pangaskaran (pengaskaran; upacara ngaskara; askara)' as the same ceremony under different name-forms -- reverses the earlier call to leave them separate. Kept upacara_ngaskara as the surviving/definition entity (broader context: Manah Tirtha Ening + Mlaspas Kajang precede it); its glossary definition was rewritten to fold in upacara_pengaskaran's own fact (Tirtha Pemanah made directly by the Sulinggih at this stage) rather than silently dropping it, per explicit instruction to merge definitions carefully.
force_merge._panebusan_penebusan_note: 2026-09-23: user asked to merge this pair, with one surviving as the definition and the other's specific content kept as a property/attribute rather than dropped or a full duplicate. Web check found 'Penebusan' (e-spelling) independently documented; 'Panebusan' (a-spelling) was not found anywhere externally, matching the same a/e dialectal-spelling pattern already known from pangabenan/pengabenan (both = ngaben). Kept 'penebusan' as the surviving/definition entity; panebusan's own two facts (SETELAH pamerasan timing, and grandeur scaling with the deceased's social rank) are preserved as attributes on the merged entity via relation_results_ngaben.normalized.json rows (S900026 already existed; S900056 added for the rank-scaling fact), not folded into the definition prose -- this REVERSES an earlier explicit decision (see S900026's own provenance note, 'item #46') to keep them separate; flagging in case that earlier call had context this pass doesn't.
force_merge._upacara_atiwa_tiwa_note: 2026-09-23 connectivity audit: 'Upacara Atiwa-Tiwa' (my drafted entry, confirmed 2026-09-22 as distinct from bare 'ngaben') was never checked against the pre-existing 'atiwa_tiwa' entity, which is the same 'seluruh rangkaian upacara penyelenggaraan jenazah' concept. Merged onto atiwa_tiwa (richer, extraction-sourced def kept), drafted glossary line removed.
force_merge._batchC_note: Batch C (2026-09-21, conersation.md items #10/#14/#15/#49): pabersihan_mati/upacara_ngelelet/upacara_melelet_pabersihan_mati/upacara_pabresihan_mati are one ritual stage under four extraction-fragmented surface names (all four Glosarium entries -- ngaben-merge-cleaned.txt lines 246/249/282/306 -- describe the identical second purification stage, aka Ngelelet/Melelet: kerik kuku + change to white clothing, sequenced after Pabersihan Hidup and before Tirtha Pangringkes). Merged onto pabersihan_mati (fullest existing definition, already carries alias 'ngelelet'). anget_angetan's DISEMBURKAN_SAAT edge and pengerikan_kuku_mutlak's DILAKUKAN_SAAT edge both already targeted 'upacara ngelelet'/'upacara "melelet" pabersihan mati' as their raw surface text, so this merge reroutes both automatically with no separate edit needed.
force_merge._batchF_note: Batch F (2026-09-21, conersation.md item #17): S271 ('adapun atiwa-tiwa yang tergolong dalam ngaben svasta adalah raçadana atau tirta yadnya pranawa... sedangkan tata pelaksanaannya sama dengan atiwa-tiwa asti vedana') says raçadana/tirta yadnya pranawa/svasta are ONE family (body unrecoverable, tirtha symbol substituted) whose PROCEDURE merely resembles Asti Vedana's (bones exhumed) -- not identity. 'tirta yadnya pranawa' was previously alias-table-merged into 'swasta', masking it as its own concept; this identity entry (checked before the alias table in Resolver.resolve(), same trick as the nistaning/madyaning/utamaning entries below) splits it back out so it can carry its own SAMA_DENGAN edges to ra_adana/swasta instead. 'toyo çarira' (S271's parenthetical for simbol tirtha, never its own concept) force-merges onto the existing simbol_tirtha node so it registers as a real alias instead of silently vanishing (its only mention was an ADALAH-LITERAL row too short to become a definition and not eligible as an attribute either). 'recadana atau swasta geni' was a stray duplicate entity created only because that compound Glosarium heading (line 201: 'Nama lain untuk Ngaben Svasta (Nywasta/Swastagni)...') never resolved to any existing id -- merged onto swasta, whose own definition was relation-sourced (S46) and had no competing Glosarium text, so this is a clean gain (an explicit corpus statement connecting Swasta to Ngaben Svasta), not a collision.
force_merge._batchE_note: Batch E (2026-09-21, conersation.md items #1/#23/#47): 'pangabenan pranawa' (Glosarium line 285) and 'pangabenan jenis pranawa' (Glosarium line 176) are the same concept under two fragmented Glosarium headings -- both definitions are near-verbatim restatements ('Jenis pe/angabenan yang dilaksanakan tanpa jenazah maupun tulang, cukup d(engan/iwakili oleh) lambang awak-awakan(ing) sawa yang dibuat dari air...'), and the source body text itself alternates between the two spellings for the same referent one paragraph apart (ngaben-merge-cleaned.txt lines 2265 'pangabenan Pranawa selalu dilakukan tanpa jenazah...' and 2271 'Supta Pranawa masih tergolong pangabenan jenis Pranawa'). Merged onto 'pangabenan jenis pranawa' (the fuller heading, and the id item #1 names as the target supta_pranawa's existing S2480 BAGIAN_DARI edge already correctly points at). 'sanghyang agni' force-merges onto the pre-existing 'hyang agni' entity (whose own definition already parenthesizes 'Sang Hyang Agni' as the same referent) -- the gazetteer lists 'sanghyang agni' as its own standalone ENTITAS_KEAGAMAAN term, so without this override a future extraction using that exact surface would silently mint a duplicate deity node instead of landing on the existing one; damar_kurung's S1136 definition ('sarana permohonan kepada sanghyang agni') already names it, so this also unblocks that edge (see relation_results_ngaben.normalized.json, real S1136).
force_merge._batchH_note: Batch H (2026-09-21, conersation.md items #13/#29, definition-only fixes). Two force_merge VALUES fixed to remove the same id_with_underscores-instead-of-spaced-name bug Batch A found and fixed on broader_overrides KEYS (see the *** 2026-09-21 correction *** paragraph on broader_overrides below) -- this time on the VALUE side, which becomes the entity's displayed 'name' verbatim (get_ent() sets e['name'] = canon straight from whichever force_merge value first creates the entity, never re-spaced): 'kelompok ini' used to point at the literal string 'kelompok_paksa_mahayana' (underscored), so the bot displayed the id itself as the name; now points at 'kelompok paksa mahayana' (slug() of both forms is identical, so the entity id itself -- kelompok_paksa_mahayana -- is unaffected, only the human-facing 'name' field). 'simbol dewi sri' and 'penggunaan anggapan' used to point at 'anggapan ani-ani atau ketam' (the Glosarium-heading spelling); repointed to 'anggapan (ani-ani atau ketam)' per item #13's explicit request for the parenthetical form the corpus's own body text uses (ngaben-merge-cleaned.txt lines 2866/3377: 'Anggapan (anai-anai atau ketam)' / "'anggapan' (ani-ani atau ketam)"), with a third new identity entry ('anggapan ani-ani atau ketam' -> 'anggapan (ani-ani atau ketam)') added so the base Glosarium-heading surface (relation_results_ngaben.normalized.json line ~8909) redirects to the same new display name too, regardless of which row processes first (slug() of the parenthesized form is confirmed identical to the id already in use, so no id/edge/broader-link changes needed anywhere else). NOTE found while here, NOT fixed (out of Batch H's explicit scope, flagged for a future near-dup batch): a separate bare 'anggapan' entity (id 'anggapan', gazetteer-resolved, def 'pisau khusus yang digunakan untuk memotong padi pada masa lalu') duplicates 'anggapan_ani_ani_atau_ketam' -- both cite the identical S3591 for their kesuburan/Dewi Sri content, textbook same-concept-two-surfaces fragmentation (same shape as pabersihan_mati/pangabenan_jenis_pranawa already merged in earlier batches), never named in conersation.md's 52 items. Likewise 'upacara_panebusan' (fixed here, item #13) vs the pre-existing 'panebusan' entity (fixed in Batch E) look like the same fragmentation shape one more time -- kept separate in this pass since #13 only asked for a definition fix, not a merge decision.
force_merge._tingkatan_ngaben_note: The 9 nistaning/madyaning/utamaning-<X> sub-tier surfaces below map to themselves (a no-op resolution) purely to WIN over normalization-ngaben.json's 'tingkatan_upacara_ngaben' concept-map bucket, which force-collapses all 9 of them (plus bare nista/madya/utama) down to just 3 canonical entities (Nista/Madya/Utama) -- force_merge is checked before the concept-map in Resolver.resolve(), so an identity entry here keeps each of the 9 as its own distinct entity instead. That concept-map collapse is left in place for the bare nista/madya/utama surfaces (still correctly landing on Nista/Madya/Utama) since those really are the same 3 entities regardless of surface spelling. Without this override, 'nistaning madya' (etc.) never got its own entity at all -- the automatic dependency-rule extractor produced zero relation rows for the source's one enumerating sentence per group (S1278/S1279/S1280 in Graphing/results/final/nerResultsNgaben/hybrid_ner_results.txt), so build_kb.py never even called get_ent() for these terms; see relation_results_ngaben.normalized.json's matching manual_addition rows (sentence_id 1275/1278/1279/1280/1490) for where they're introduced. 'tingkatan ngaben' is a separate, smaller fix: a plain alias so a user asking 'apa saja tingkatan ngaben' lands on the existing tingkatan_upacara entity instead of the unrelated fuzzy hits it produced before ('tingkatan upacara' and 'tingkatan ngaben' share only one of three words).
force_merge._batchI_note: Batch I (2026-09-21, conersation.md items #4/#11/#44/#48, last content batch). Item #4 ('ngaben_madya' doesn't exist): investigation found the nista/madya/utama x nista/madya/utama tingkatan-upacara grid this item's investigation note anticipated was ALREADY fully built and connected (tingkatan_upacara hub + nista/madya/utama + all 9 nistaning/madyaning/utamaning-<X> sub-tiers, all with correct broader links, all citing real pipeline sentence_ids S1275/S1278/S1279/S1280/S1490) -- confirmed via entities.json and relation_results_ngaben.normalized.json's existing 'manual_addition+tingkatan_ngaben_fix' tagged rows, a prior session's work predating this graph-fix plan's Batch A-H (not one of the lettered batches; likely done alongside the 2026-09 'expanded glossary' commits). No hub construction was needed here. What WAS still missing: a user literally typing 'ngaben madya' had no deterministic path to the 'madya' entity (fuzzy-match dependent) -- the four entries below are plain resolution-convenience aliases, same shape as the pre-existing 'tingkatan ngaben' -> 'tingkatan upacara' entry directly above. 'ngaben ngewangun' -> utama is real corpus terminology, not a made-up convenience form: ngaben-merge-cleaned.txt lines 2790/3627/3677 use 'Ngaben Ngewangun' interchangeably with 'Upacara Ngaben Utama' (e.g. line 3627: 'tingkat Upacara Ngaben Utama (Ngaben Ngewangun)'); none of these four sentences were ever assigned a pipeline sentence_id, so no relation_results_ngaben.normalized.json row was added for them -- they are resolver config, not graph edges, consistent with how the pre-existing 'tingkatan ngaben' alias above was handled. Items #11/#44/#48: 'kepercayaan setempat' fixed above (was 'upacara_mesulub', underscored -- same force_merge-VALUE-becomes-displayed-name bug Batch H fixed on 'kelompok ini'/'simbol dewi sri', now fixed here too); 'upacara meselub'/'upacara suluban' are the corpus's own alternate spellings for upacara_mesulub (ngaben-merge-cleaned.txt lines 3681/3684). 'ngwangun'/'ngeplugin' are corpus-confirmed alternate names for ngulapin, not synonyms I invented (line 1537: 'Upacara ini dinamakan juga Ngwangun... Dinamakan pula Ngeplugin...' -- both explicitly 'dinamakan juga'/'dinamakan pula' the same upacara). 'ngroras jenis kangsen' is ngangsen's own corpus-given alternate name (line 2348: 'diadakanlah upacara darurat selaku pengganti, bernama Ngangsen atau melaksanakan upacara Ngroras jenis Kangsen').
force_merge._review_queue_2026_09_23_note: user's manual review_queue.jsonl pass over the fragment_entity items: 'nama upanisad' is just the existing upanisad entity with a leading 'nama' (name) word the extractor failed to strip -- force_merge it straight onto 'upanisad' rather than adding a strip_modifiers rule (a shared-code change with a bigger blast radius for one observed case). 'perwujudan sredaning cita' is a genuine new concept (sincerity/wholehearted intent behind an offering, S1163/S1361/S3004 all use spelling variants -- sredaning manah/sredaning citta/sredaning cita -- but only this one occurrence is ENTITY-typed rather than a LITERAL attribute, so it's the only one that needed a merge target) -- force_merge onto 'sredaning cita'; its S3004 ADALAH relation ('wujud dari ketulus-ikhlasan hati pihak yang bersangkutan') becomes its definition automatically once merged, no glossary edit needed.

_keep_distinct_note: never collapse these into their head word via modifier-strip; they may still get a broader: <head> link.
_type_overrides_note_2026_09_23: The nine nistaning/madyaning/utamaning-<X> sub-tiers were auto-typed TAHAPAN_UPACARA (ceremony stage) by the labels-vote heuristic, but they're classification TIERS (like nista/madya/utama themselves, already KONSEP_HUKUM_ADAT), not sequential stages -- confirmed live: the bot called utamaning_utama a 'tahapan upacara' when asked about sawa_wedana, which is a tier label the corpus applies to it, not a step it passes through. Retyped to match their parent's type.
_bad_definition_note: Sentence ids whose BERARTI/ADALAH relation gives a WRONG or context-free definition for the subject entity build_kb.py resolves it to -- mis-attributed subject/context, not just a weak one. S2003 actually describes 'wadah', not 'bade' (the subject it landed on); S2056 ('ciri paksa brahmanisme') is a near-meaningless fragment attached to 'patulangan'. build_kb.py skips these as a definition candidate so the bot doesn't present them as authoritative. Left null until a proper hand-authored Glosarium entry replaces them -- see Graphing/kb/glossary_draft_review_batch2.md.

broader_overrides._catur_wangsa_note: 2026-09-23 connectivity audit: 'wangsa_sudra_jadma' already auto-linked to 'wangsa' (multi-word head heuristic caught it), but the other 3 catur-wangsa castes are single-word so the heuristic never fires for them, same shape as Panca Maha Bhuta's elements. wangsa's own definition explicitly names all 4 (Brahmana/Ksatria/Wesia/Sudra) plus clan lines like Pasek as things it covers, so all 4 castes + Pasek are linked here.
broader_overrides._yadnya_family_note: 2026-09-23: dewa_yadnya's own definition (and panca_yadnya's) explicitly enumerate it as one of the five Panca Yadnya -- same enumerated-hub shape as Panca Maha Bhuta/Panca Dewata. 2026-09-23 semantics-fix pass: bhuta_yadnya/pitra_yadnya used to be left pointing at the automatic heuristic's pick ('bhuta'/'pitra') per the note this replaces -- but both entities' own definitions say the same 'salah satu dari Panca Yadnya' thing dewa_yadnya's does, so re-parented to panca_yadnya for consistency (a ritual can't be 'a type of' the deity/soul-concept it's for).
broader_overrides._pengawak_family_note: 2026-09-23: isi_pengawak ('pengawak's filling', a collective/generic term) and kekitir (one specific named filling item, per its own definition 'salah satu isian pengawak') are both components of pengawak, not independent concepts -- same compositional-hub shape as the pangringkes family.
broader_overrides._associative_stage_links_note: 2026-09-23: these each explicitly name ONE specific parent ceremony/object in their own definition (a stated part-of/used-during fact, not just a passing mention among several candidates) -- sambungan_kain_putih is a named feature of kain_putih itself; tumpeng is explicitly stated to be a form of ayaban. Isolated candidates with multiple, ambiguous, or merely co-occurring references (the majority of the 77) were deliberately left alone -- see connectivity_report.md, this is not an exhaustive pass. bangbang_rare/boreh/pangenteg_linggih/mlaspas_kajang used to be here too, but 'part-of/used-during' isn't 'is-a' -- TERMASUK_JENIS misstated all four (a burial pit isn't 'a type of' the rite it's dug for, an ointment isn't 'a type of' the bathing stage it's used in). Moved to broader_suppress + an explicit BAGIAN_DARI/DILAKUKAN_SAAT relation each, 2026-09-23 semantics-fix pass (see broader_suppress note).
broader_overrides._semantics_fix_note_2026_09_23: pabersihan_mati/tarpana/ayaban_upakara_diuskamaligi/mapegat used to point 'ngaben' here too, and tirta_pengeringkes used to point 'pangringkes' (wrong -- a holy water can't be 'a type of' a ceremony stage, moved to 'tirtha' above, its real category). The first four are genuine stages IN ngaben (each says so in its own definition: 'tahapan dalam upacara Ngaben' / 'bagian dari rangkaian upacara'), which TERMASUK_JENIS misstates as 'is a type of ngaben' -- exactly the mapegat bug the user reported 2026-09-23. _exclude_note:
Entity ids the bot must never resolve a user query to or list under a type category -- generic/ambiguous words the extractor over-eagerly turned into standalone entities (see Graphing/kb/glossary_draft_review.md). 'manusia' is just the common word 'human' pulled from one philosophical sentence; 'badan' ('body') is used for 3 unrelated things in the source text (a philosophy term, a specific ritual effigy, and generic body) so no single merge target would be correct. 'ngroras' is a near-empty duplicate of the now-well-defined 'ngerorasin' -- excluded here (not just force_merge'd) because its own name would otherwise exact-match before force_merge is ever consulted (exact-match is checked first in kb_resolver.resolve()); excluding it from the surface map lets the 'ngroras' -> 'ngerorasin' force_merge entry actually fire. Kept in entities.json/the graph for structural completeness -- read by kb_resolver.py only, which filters excluded ids out of every bot-facing surface (exact/alias/fuzzy resolution, type listings, search).

The 2026-09-17 glossary-completion pass (closing entities.json's then-89 null-definition entities) added the large batch above: each is a rule-extractor fragment with NO single clean alias target -- a generic anaphoric reference ('sarana-sarana tersebut', 'semua sarana', 'keluarga/masyarakat'), a full clause/temporal-purpose phrase ('setelah tirtha dipercikkan', 'tergesa-gesa memandikan jenazah'), or a two-entity coordination ('sesajen dan punjung') -- so unlike the batch's other findings (see force_merge above, and broader_overrides for the true near-duplicates), inventing either a definition or a single merge target for these would misrepresent them. They stay in the graph, undefined, but are excluded here so the bot's own resolver never surfaces or answers about them directly. NOTE: this list alone does NOT stop one of these ids from appearing as an unexplained relationship target inside another (defined) entity's answer -- exclude_from_resolution is read only by kb_resolver.py (bot-side query resolution), never by build_kb.py at KB-build time (confirmed by reading build_kb.py directly -- it has no reference to this key at all). A handful of these fragments do have exactly one incoming relation edge (that's literally how the extractor created them, as the object of one triple) and could still surface as a bare, undefined name in that edge's target/context. Closing that residual gap for good needs either a review_decisions.json reject/fix keyed to each fragment's originating sentence_id (see review_decisions.json's own note on the entity-creation-loop gate) or a dedicated Cypher/actions.py-side filter -- deliberately left as a follow-up, not attempted here, since guessing sentence ids for ~34 fragments without reading each one's exact origin line risks silently rejecting the wrong triple.
